# Projects & promptise run

A Promptise project works like a Node project. `promptise.toml` plays the part of `package.json`: it names the program (`main`), lists named commands (`[scripts]`), and says which environment variables the project needs (`[env]`). `promptise run` runs your program the way `node` or `npm start` would.

Your program stays a normal Python program. Flags add dev tools, a terminal UI, file watching, production behavior or an HTTP API, and with them every agent the program builds is instrumented, with no changes to your code.

```bash
promptise init --project my-bot     # create a project
cd my-bot
cp .env.example .env                # then set OPENAI_API_KEY in .env

promptise run                       # run main.py, like `python main.py`
promptise run --devtools            # live traces, tool calls, tokens and cost
promptise run --tui                 # the full terminal UI
promptise run --serve               # an HTTP API for the agent
promptise run --prod                # JSON logs, preflight checks, graceful SIGTERM
```

A complete example project is in [`examples/run/support_bot/`](https://github.com/promptise-com/foundry/tree/main/examples/run/support_bot).

!!! note "`promptise run` and `promptise runtime`"
    `promptise run` runs your Python program. For long-running agents that react to triggers (cron, webhooks, file changes) and are declared in `.agent` manifests, use the [Agent Runtime](../runtime/index.md): `promptise runtime start agents/ --detach`, then `promptise runtime status`, `logs`, `rewind` and `stop` from any terminal. See the [Runtime CLI](../runtime/cli.md).

---

## How it maps to npm

| Node / npm | Promptise |
|---|---|
| `package.json` | `promptise.toml`, or `[tool.promptise]` in `pyproject.toml` |
| `"main": "index.js"` | `main = "main.py"` |
| `"scripts": {...}` | `[scripts]` |
| `node index.js` | `python main.py` |
| `npm start` | `promptise run` (or `promptise run start`, if you define a `start` script) |
| `npm run dev` | `promptise run dev` |
| `npm run` (lists scripts) | `promptise run --list` |
| `npm init` | `promptise init --project` |
| `nodemon` | `promptise run --watch` |

The manifest describes how to *run* the project. The agent itself stays in your Python code.

---

## Create a project

```bash
promptise init --project [DIR] [--name NAME] [--model MODEL] [--force]
```

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `DIR` | Where to create the project (default: the current directory). Created if missing. |
| `--name NAME` | The project name (default: the directory's name). |
| `--model MODEL` | The model string the agent uses (default: `openai:gpt-5-mini`). It also decides which API key `[env] required` lists: `anthropic:...` gives `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, a local `ollama:...` needs none, and a string without a known provider prefix gives `OPENAI_API_KEY`. |
| `--force` | Overwrite files that already exist. |

It writes:

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `promptise.toml` | `name`, `version = "0.1.0"`, `description`, `main = "main.py"`, `agent = "agent.py:create_agent"`, the scripts `dev`, `ui`, `start`, `serve` and `check`, `[env] required`, and a commented-out `[pricing]` example |
| `agent.py` | `create_agent`, the agent factory, with one local tool (`add`) |
| `main.py` | A normal script: builds the agent, asks the question from its arguments (or a default one), prints the answer and shuts the agent down |
| `.env.example` | The variables the model's provider needs |
| `README.md` | How to run the project |
| `.gitignore` | `.env`, `.promptise/` and `__pycache__/`, added to an existing file without duplicating lines |

`promptise init --project` never overwrites a file without `--force`. When files exist, it lists every one of them and writes nothing. It never touches the network.

`promptise init` without `--project` still writes a `.superagent` template, as before. See the [CLI reference](cli.md#promptise-init-generate-a-template-or-a-project).

---

## A project, file by file

This is what `promptise init --project` creates (comments shortened).

`promptise.toml`:

```toml
name = "my-bot"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "An agent built with Promptise"
main = "main.py"                  # the program `promptise run` runs
agent = "agent.py:create_agent"   # the agent factory for --serve, -i and chat mode

[scripts]
dev = "promptise run --devtools --watch"
ui = "promptise run --tui"
start = "promptise run --prod"
serve = "promptise run --serve"
check = "promptise run --prod --check"

[env]
files = [".env"]
required = ["OPENAI_API_KEY"]
```

`agent.py`, the agent factory:

```python
from __future__ import annotations

from promptise import PromptiseAgent, build_agent, tool
from promptise.run import RunContext

MODEL = "openai:gpt-5-mini"


@tool
def add(a: float, b: float) -> float:
    """Add two numbers and return the sum."""
    return a + b


async def create_agent(ctx: RunContext | None = None) -> PromptiseAgent:
    model = (ctx.model if ctx is not None else None) or MODEL
    return await build_agent(
        model=model,
        instructions="You are a helpful assistant. Use the add tool for arithmetic.",
        extra_tools=[add],
    )
```

`main.py`, the program:

```python
from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import sys

from agent import create_agent


async def main() -> None:
    question = " ".join(sys.argv[1:]) or "What is 1234 + 5678?"
    agent = await create_agent()
    messages = [{"role": "user", "content": question}]
    try:
        result = await agent.ainvoke({"messages": messages})
        print(result["messages"][-1].content)
    finally:
        await agent.shutdown()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

`python main.py` and `promptise run` run the same program. With `promptise run`, the project's `.env` and `[env]` settings are applied, and the agent shows up in the dev tools and the terminal UI.

---

## The manifest

### Where `promptise run` finds it

`promptise run` looks in the current directory, then in each parent directory. It stops at the first directory that has a `promptise.toml`, or a `pyproject.toml` with a `[tool.promptise]` table. In the same directory, `promptise.toml` wins. The search also stops at the repository root (the first directory that holds `.git`), so a manifest above your repository is never used.

`-f PATH` / `--manifest PATH` names the manifest explicitly.

The **project root** is the manifest's directory. Relative paths in the manifest are relative to it.

Without a manifest, `promptise run some_file.py` still works: the root is the current directory and every setting has its default.

A manifest decides what runs, so `promptise run` only uses one found this way if it is a regular file owned by you that other users cannot write (the same rule as for `.env` files). A `promptise.toml` planted in a shared directory such as `/tmp` is refused with an error. `-f/--manifest` uses the file you name.

### A full example

```toml
name = "support-bot"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Answers support tickets"
main = "main.py"
agent = "agent.py:create_agent"
python_path = ["."]

[scripts]
dev = "promptise run --devtools --watch"
ui = "promptise run --tui"
start = "promptise run --prod"
eval = "python evals/run.py"

[env]
files = [".env"]
required = ["OPENAI_API_KEY"]
vars = { LOG_LEVEL = "info" }

[dev]
observe = "full"
watch = ["."]
ignore = ["data/*"]
report = ".promptise/last-run.json"

[prod]
log_format = "json"
log_level = "INFO"
observe = "off"
shutdown_timeout = 30

[serve]
host = "127.0.0.1"
port = 8080
auth_token_env = "PROMPTISE_SERVE_TOKEN"
max_concurrency = 8

[pricing]
"gpt-5-mini*" = { input = 0.25, output = 2.0 }
```

Every key is optional. An empty `promptise.toml` is a valid manifest.

### Top-level keys

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | the root directory's name | The project name, shown in the dev tools, the TUI and `/v1/info`. |
| `version` | string | none | The project version. |
| `description` | string | none | A one-line description. |
| `main` | string | the first existing of `main.py`, `agent.py`, `app.py` | The program `promptise run` runs, relative to the root. |
| `agent` | string | none | An agent factory for the chat, once and serve modes: `file.py:function` or `package.module:function`. |
| `python_path` | list of strings | `["."]` | Directories added to `sys.path`, relative to the root. The run and `--check` both use them to import the agent factory. |

### `[scripts]`

A table of named commands, like npm scripts. Each key is a script name and each value is a command line. A name may not be empty, start with `-` or contain spaces, and a command may not be empty. See [Scripts](#scripts).

### `[env]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `files` | list of strings | `[".env"]` | `.env`-style files to load, in order, relative to the root. A missing file is skipped. |
| `required` | list of strings | `[]` | Variables that must be set before the program starts. Every missing one is reported at once. |
| `vars` | table of strings | `{}` | Default values, set only when the variable is not set already. |

See [Environment variables](#environment-variables) for the loading rules.

### `[dev]`

Applies with `--devtools`, `--tui` and `--watch`.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `observe` | `basic`, `standard` or `full` | `full` | How much is recorded for agents that set no `observe` of their own. `--observe LEVEL` overrides it. |
| `watch` | list of strings | `["."]` | Paths `--watch` watches, relative to the root. |
| `ignore` | list of strings | `[]` | Extra glob patterns `--watch` ignores. `.git`, `__pycache__`, `.venv`, `venv`, `node_modules`, `.promptise`, `.mypy_cache`, `.pytest_cache` and `.ruff_cache` are always ignored. |
| `report` | string | `""` | Write a JSON run report to this path (relative to the project root) when the run ends. Empty means no report. `--report PATH` overrides it; that path is relative to the directory you run the command from. |

### `[prod]`

Applies with `--prod`.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `log_format` | `json` or `text` | `json` | `json` writes one JSON object per log line on stderr. |
| `log_level` | `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARNING`, `ERROR` or `CRITICAL` | `INFO` | The root log level (case does not matter). |
| `observe` | `off`, `basic`, `standard` or `full` | `off` | Record agent activity at this level for agents that set no `observe` of their own. Each timeline event becomes a JSON log line. |
| `shutdown_timeout` | number (seconds) | `30` | How long in-flight work may take to finish after SIGTERM. |

### `[serve]`

Applies with `--serve`. The serve mode needs an agent factory (`agent`, or a `file.py:factory` target).

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `host` | string | `127.0.0.1` | The address to listen on. `--host` overrides it. |
| `port` | integer, 0 to 65535 | `8080` | The port. `--port` / `-p` overrides it. |
| `auth_token_env` | string | `PROMPTISE_SERVE_TOKEN` | The environment variable that holds the bearer token clients must send. A token is required when `host` is not a loopback address. |
| `max_concurrency` | integer, 1 or more | `8` | Requests answered at the same time. More get `429`. |

### `[pricing]`

Prices for the cost estimates in the dev tools, the TUI and the run report, in USD per one million tokens. Keys are model names, and `fnmatch` globs are allowed:

```toml
[pricing]
"gpt-5-mini*" = { input = 0.25, output = 2.0 }
"claude-sonnet-4-5" = { input = 3.0, output = 15.0 }
```

A model matches by its exact name first, then by its name without the `provider:` prefix, then against each glob in table order. Both `input` and `output` are required and must be 0 or more.

Promptise has no built-in price list. Prices change, and a wrong number is worse than none. A model without a price shows `—` instead of a cost and is listed as unpriced. The numbers above are examples: check your provider's current prices.

### In `pyproject.toml`

Put the same keys under `[tool.promptise]`, and the sub-tables under `[tool.promptise.<name>]`:

```toml
[tool.promptise]
name = "support-bot"
main = "main.py"
agent = "support_bot.agent:create_agent"

[tool.promptise.scripts]
dev = "promptise run --devtools --watch"

[tool.promptise.env]
required = ["OPENAI_API_KEY"]
```

### Mistakes are errors

An unknown key is an error, so a typo does not go unnoticed. The message names the file and the dotted path of every problem:

```text
/work/support-bot/promptise.toml:
  - dev.obsrve: unknown key (check the spelling)
  - serve.port: Input should be less than or equal to 65535
```

In `pyproject.toml`, the paths start with `tool.promptise.`. `promptise run` exits with code 2 on a manifest error.

### Read a manifest from Python

The loader `promptise run` uses is public in `promptise.run`, for tools and tests
that need the project's settings:

```python
from pathlib import Path
from promptise.run import ManifestError, find_manifest, load_manifest

path = find_manifest(Path.cwd())   # nearest promptise.toml or [tool.promptise], or None
if path is not None:
    try:
        manifest = load_manifest(path)
        print(manifest.name, manifest.main, sorted(manifest.scripts))
    except ManifestError as exc:
        print("\n".join(exc.problems))
```

| Name | What it does |
|---|---|
| `find_manifest(start=None)` | The nearest manifest from `start` (default: the working directory) upwards, or `None`. In each directory `promptise.toml` wins over a `pyproject.toml` with `[tool.promptise]`. The search stops at the first directory holding `.git`. |
| `load_manifest(path)` | Read and validate the file and return a `ProjectManifest` (`name`, `version`, `description`, `main`, `agent`, `python_path`, `scripts`, `env`, `dev`, `prod`, `serve`, `pricing`, `path`, `root`). |
| `ManifestError` | Raised when the file cannot be read, parsed or validated; `problems` lists one line per problem. |

---

## `main` and the agent factory

A project can name two things: a program (`main`) and an agent factory (`agent`).

- **`main`** is your program. It does whatever your application does: answer a batch of tickets, run a pipeline, start a bot. `promptise run` runs it like `python main.py`.
- **`agent`** is a function that builds and returns one agent. `promptise run` uses it when *it* drives the agent: the interactive chat, a one-shot question (`-i`) and the HTTP API (`--serve`).

Most projects have both: `main.py` imports the factory from `agent.py`, so the program and the HTTP API use the same agent.

### `main`: your program

`promptise run` runs `main` as a complete program, with the same semantics as `python main.py`:

- It runs as `__main__`, so `if __name__ == "__main__":` blocks run.
- `sys.argv` is `[main, *ARGS]`: the arguments after the target.
- `sys.path[0]` is the main file's directory, followed by the root and the `python_path` entries.
- The working directory is the project root when a manifest was found. The directory you ran `promptise run` from is in `PROMPTISE_INIT_CWD`.
- `sys.exit(code)` sets the exit code. Ctrl+C gives 130. An uncaught exception gives 1 (with a readable traceback in dev mode).

Every agent the program builds with `build_agent()` is instrumented: it appears in the dev tools, the TUI and the run report. See [What promptise run adds](#what-promptise-run-adds-to-your-agents).

### The agent factory

A factory is a function that returns a `PromptiseAgent`. It may be sync or async, and it takes either no argument or a `RunContext`:

```python
from promptise import PromptiseAgent, build_agent
from promptise.run import RunContext


async def create_agent(ctx: RunContext) -> PromptiseAgent:
    return await build_agent(model=ctx.model or "openai:gpt-5-mini", instructions="...")
```

A factory that also runs outside `promptise run` (called from `main.py`, say) can make the context optional: `async def create_agent(ctx: RunContext | None = None)`. `promptise run` still passes the context.

The factory must build the agent when it is called. If the name points to an agent that was already built when the module was imported, `promptise run` refuses it with a message that says so, because it must build the agent inside its own event loop. `promptise run` calls `await agent.shutdown()` when the run ends.

`RunContext` is a frozen dataclass in `promptise.run`:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `project` | `str` | The project name. |
| `root` | `Path` | The project root. |
| `mode` | `"script"`, `"chat"`, `"once"` or `"serve"` | The mode of this run. |
| `devtools` | `bool` | `--devtools` (or `--tui`) is on. |
| `prod` | `bool` | `--prod` is on. |
| `tui` | `bool` | The run is shown in the terminal UI. |
| `model` | `str` or `None` | The `--model` override. `promptise run` applies it to every agent anyway, so a factory only needs it to pick a model-specific setting. |
| `manifest` | `ProjectManifest` or `None` | The parsed manifest. |
| `args` | `tuple[str, ...]` | The arguments after the target. |

---

## Targets and modes

```bash
promptise run [TARGET] [ARGS]... [OPTIONS]
```

`TARGET` is one of these, checked in this order:

1. Omitted: the manifest's `main`.
2. A name in `[scripts]`: run that script. See [Scripts](#scripts).
3. A `.py` file: run that file instead of `main`, with the manifest's settings.
4. `file.py:factory` or `package.module:factory`: use that agent factory.

`ARGS` become the program's `sys.argv[1:]`. To pass arguments to `main`, name the file:

```bash
promptise run main.py "Where is my order A1002?"
```

Put `--` before arguments that look like `promptise run` options, so they reach your program unchanged: `promptise run main.py -- --verbose`.

### Modes

| Mode | What runs | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| `script` | The program, as `__main__` | Running your application |
| `chat` | The factory's agent, in an interactive chat in the terminal | Trying the agent by hand |
| `once` | The factory's agent, for one question; the answer is printed and the process exits | Shell scripts, CI checks |
| `serve` | The factory's agent, behind an [HTTP API](#serve-mode) | Other services calling the agent |

`--mode auto` (the default) picks the mode:

1. An explicit `:factory` target, `--serve` or `-i` gives an agent mode (`chat`, `serve` or `once`).
2. Otherwise, if the main file has an `if __name__ == "__main__":` block, or top-level statements other than imports, definitions and assignments (`asyncio.run(main())`), it runs as a **script**.
3. Otherwise, if it defines `create_agent`, it opens the **chat**.
4. Otherwise it runs as a script.

Set the mode yourself with `--mode script|chat|once|serve`. `--serve` is short for `--mode serve`, and `-i TEXT` / `--input TEXT` is short for `--mode once` with that question.

### Chat mode

```bash
promptise run --mode chat                 # the manifest's agent factory
promptise run agent.py:create_agent       # a factory named on the command line
```

The answer streams as it is written, and tool calls appear inline. Commands:

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/help` | List the commands |
| `/stats` | Tokens, cost and tool calls so far |
| `/tools` | The agent's tools |
| `/reset` | Start a new conversation |
| `/exit` | Quit (also Ctrl+D) |

### Once mode

```bash
promptise run -i "Where is my order A1002?"
echo "Where is my order A1002?" | promptise run -i -     # read the question from stdin
promptise run -i "Where is my order A1002?" --json       # the answer and stats as JSON
```

---

## What promptise run adds to your agents

A plain `promptise run` of a script adds nothing to your agents: the program runs exactly as with `python main.py`, plus the project's environment, at no extra cost.

With `--devtools`, `--tui`, `--model`, `--observe`, `--report` or `[prod] observe`, and in the chat, once and serve modes, `promptise run` installs a harness before your program starts. `build_agent()` asks it for settings and reports every agent it builds. With the harness, `promptise run`:

- turns on observability, at the run's level, for agents that set no `observe` of their own, without writing report files;
- gives each agent an id (`agent`, `agent-2`, ...) when it has none;
- adds a sink for agent events, creating an `EventNotifier` when the agent has none;
- replaces every agent's model with the `--model` override, when you give one;
- reports each agent's model, tools, MCP servers and features to the dev tools and the TUI.

Your values always win. An agent built with `observe=False` stays unobserved. One with its own `observe` config keeps it, and its own `events` notifier keeps working, with the run's sink added to it.

Outside `promptise run`, nothing changes: `python main.py` builds the same agents with no harness.

---

## Scripts

`[scripts]` holds named commands, like npm scripts:

```toml
[scripts]
dev = "promptise run --devtools --watch"
ui = "promptise run --tui"
start = "promptise run --prod"
eval = "python evals/run.py"
lint = "ruff check ."
```

```bash
promptise run dev           # promptise run --devtools --watch
promptise run eval smoke    # python evals/run.py smoke
promptise run --list        # list the scripts
```

- A script runs through the shell, from the project root. Its exit code is the exit code of `promptise run`.
- Arguments after the script name are appended to the command. Put `--` before arguments that look like `promptise run` options: `promptise run eval -- --limit 10`.
- `promptise run` options given with the script name are passed on when the script is itself a `promptise` command: `promptise run dev --model anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-5` runs `promptise run --devtools --watch --model anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-5`. For any other command they are ignored, with a warning.
- The directory of the Python that runs `promptise` comes first on `PATH`, so `python`, `pytest` and `promptise` in a script are the ones from the same environment. This works like `node_modules/.bin` in npm.
- The script gets `PROMPTISE_RUN_SCRIPT` (its name), `PROMPTISE_PROJECT_ROOT` and `PROMPTISE_INIT_CWD` (the directory you ran `promptise run` from).
- `[env]` is applied by `promptise run` itself, so a script that runs `promptise run` gets it. Other commands get the environment you started with.
- A script that calls itself through `promptise run` stops with an error instead of looping forever.
- When the command is echoed, the values of `--env KEY=VALUE` are shown as `***`.
- On Windows, scripts run through `cmd.exe`, which has no quoting that is safe for every character: an appended argument that contains `& | < > ^ % ! "` is refused. Run such a command directly.

---

## Environment variables

Before the program starts, `promptise run` sets up its environment:

1. **Command line.** `-e K=V` / `--env K=V` (repeatable) sets a variable for this run. It wins over everything, including a variable already set in your shell.
2. **Files.** The `--env-file PATH` files (repeatable) load first, then the `[env] files` (default `[".env"]`), in order. A missing `--env-file` is an error; a missing file in `[env] files` is skipped.
3. **Defaults.** `[env] vars` fills in variables that are still not set.
4. **Check.** Every variable in `[env] required` must be set. If any are missing, `promptise run` lists all of them and exits with code 2.

The rules:

- **A file never overrides.** A variable that is already set to a non-empty value is never changed by a file or by `[env] vars`, so the first file that sets a variable wins. A variable exported as an empty string (`export OPENAI_API_KEY=`) counts as not set, so a file's value fills it.
- **Unsafe files are refused.** A file must be a regular file. On Linux and macOS it must be owned by you and not writable by other users. An unsafe or unreadable file is an error that names the file.
- **`PROMPTISE_NO_DOTENV=1` turns file loading off.** No `.env`-style file is loaded. Use it in containers and CI, where the environment is set from outside.

The CLI also loads a `.env` from the current directory (or a parent, up to the project root) before any command runs, under the same rules. The folder holding `promptise.toml` is a project root, so a project nested in another repository never reads that repository's `.env`; list it in `[env] files` (`["../.env"]`) to use it on purpose. See [Configuration & Secrets](../getting-started/configuration.md).

`promptise run` never shows variable values. The TUI and the run report list only whether each variable is set.

---

## Dev tools

```bash
promptise run --devtools     # or -d
```

`--devtools` prints a live trace of every agent on stderr. Your program's own output stays on stdout, unchanged. The trace shows:

- each agent as it is built: its model and tools;
- every LLM turn: model, latency, tokens, estimated cost and the tools it asked for;
- every tool call, with its arguments and a preview of the result;
- errors and notable agent events (a guardrail block, a slow tool, an approval request).

When the run ends, a summary table lists the totals per agent, per model and per tool: LLM calls, tokens, tool calls, errors, latency and cost.

<figure markdown>
  <img class="screenshot" src="../../assets/run/devtools.svg" alt="promptise run --devtools on the support bot example: the agent is built, the LLM asks for lookup_order, the tool returns the order, the answer is printed, and the summary lists 2 LLM calls, 1,632 tokens and a cost of $0.0005." />
  <figcaption><code>promptise run --devtools</code> on the support bot example. The trace goes to stderr; the program's answer is its own output.</figcaption>
</figure>

| Setting | Effect |
|---|---|
| `[dev] observe` / `--observe LEVEL` | How much is recorded: `basic`, `standard` or `full` (default). |
| `[dev] report` / `--report PATH` | Write a JSON run report on exit: every run event that was kept, and the final totals. |
| `[pricing]` | The prices behind the cost estimates. |

Costs are estimates from your `[pricing]` table. A model without a price shows `—`.

---

## Watch mode

```bash
promptise run --watch            # or -w
promptise run --devtools --watch # the `dev` script of a new project
```

`--watch` runs the program in a child process and restarts it when a project file changes, like `nodemon`. Changes are debounced, so saving several files restarts once. When the program exits on its own, `promptise run` waits for the next change and runs it again. `--watch` is for development: it cannot be combined with `--prod`.

- Watched: the paths in `[dev] watch` (default: the whole root).
- File types: `.py`, `.toml`, `.yaml`, `.yml`, `.json`, `.md`, `.txt`, `.env`, `.j2`, `.jinja`, `.agent` and `.superagent`.
- Ignored: `.git`, `__pycache__`, `.venv`, `venv`, `node_modules`, `.promptise`, `.mypy_cache`, `.pytest_cache`, `.ruff_cache`, and the globs in `[dev] ignore`.

---

## The terminal UI

```bash
promptise run --tui      # also -t or -tui
promptise run ui         # the `ui` script of a new project
```

`--tui` opens a full-screen terminal UI. It records what `--devtools` records and shows it in tabs. The program runs in a child process, and its output is captured line by line, so nothing it prints draws over the UI.

In script mode, the first tab is a console: it shows the program's output, and a line you type is sent to the program's standard input. In the agent modes (`--mode chat`, `--serve`), the first tab is a chat with the agent.

<figure markdown>
  <img class="screenshot" src="../../assets/run/tui-chat-approved.svg" alt="The Chat tab: three support tickets, each answer with the tool calls it made inline (lookup_order, search_help_center, open_ticket), their arguments, results and timings. The header shows 7 LLM calls, 6,188 tokens and a cost of $0.0019." />
  <figcaption>The Chat tab of the support bot example (<code>promptise run --tui --mode chat</code>). Tool calls show inline, with their arguments, results and timings.</figcaption>
</figure>

| Key | Tab | Shows |
|---|---|---|
| `1` | Console / Chat | The program's output and input, or the chat with the agent (streamed answers, tool calls inline) |
| `2` | Trace | Every timeline entry of every agent (LLM calls, tool calls and results, errors, with timings), filterable by agent, with the full entry beside it |
| `3` | Tools | Every tool call (arguments, result, latency) and the tools each agent has |
| `4` | Metrics | Totals, per agent, model and tool, and the tokens of each LLM call |
| `5` | Events | Agent events: invocations, slow tools, guardrails, approvals |
| `6` | Approvals | Tool calls waiting for a human decision, and the decisions made |
| `7` | Agents | Every agent the program built: model, observability level, tools, MCP servers, features and instructions |
| `8` | MCP | The MCP servers the agents use, with their transport and tools |
| `9` | Logs | Python log records and the program's stderr, filterable by level |
| `0` | Run | The project, the entry, the mode and flags, the manifest, the environment variables (set or missing, never their values), the scripts, HTTP requests in serve mode, and the run's state and exit code |

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `0` to `9` | Switch tabs (when the input box does not have focus) |
| `esc` | Leave the input box |
| `r` | Restart the program |
| `s` | Stop the program |
| `a` / `d` | Approvals tab: approve or deny the selected request (deny asks for an optional reason) |
| `a` | Trace tab: filter by agent |
| `l` | Logs tab: filter by level |
| `?` | Help |
| `q`, Ctrl+C | Quit |

</figure>

<figure markdown>
  <img class="screenshot" src="../../assets/run/tui-metrics.svg" alt="The Metrics tab: LLM calls, prompt and completion tokens, cost, tool calls, errors, latency p50 and p95, tokens per LLM call as a chart, and tables per agent, model and tool." />

The Approvals tab answers requests from agents whose approval policy uses a `QueueApprovalHandler`. Other handlers (webhooks, callbacks) already have someone answering them and are left alone. See [Approval (HITL)](approval.md).

Add `--watch` (`promptise run --tui --watch`) and the program restarts in the UI whenever a watched file changes; the run history stays, and each run is numbered.

`--tui` needs an interactive terminal. It cannot be combined with `--prod`.

---

## Production

```bash
promptise run --prod            # or `promptise run start` in a new project
promptise run --prod --check    # check the project, then exit
```

`--prod` is for running the project unattended, in a container or under a process manager.

- **JSON logs on stderr.** Every log record becomes one JSON object per line: `ts`, `level`, `logger`, `msg`, and any extra fields (`exc` for a traceback). Stdout stays your program's output. Set `[prod] log_format = "text"` for plain lines and `[prod] log_level` for the level.
- **Run events in the logs.** The start and the end of the run are written as JSON log lines (`"logger": "promptise.run.events"`). When agents are instrumented (in serve mode, or with `[prod] observe` set), so are every agent built and closed, every HTTP request, and the final totals. With `[prod] observe`, every timeline event (LLM calls, tool calls, errors) is written too.
- **Checks before the start.** See [Preflight checks](#preflight-checks). Under `--prod`, the problems are written as one JSON log line (`"msg": "preflight failed"`, `"problems": [...]`).
- **Graceful SIGTERM.** On SIGTERM, a script shuts down the way it does on Ctrl+C: it sees `KeyboardInterrupt`, `asyncio.run` cancels its main task, `finally` blocks run and agents shut down. The exit code is 143. In serve mode the server drains instead (see [Limits and shutdown](#limits-and-shutdown)) and exits with 0. A second SIGTERM exits at once.

`--prod` cannot be combined with `--tui` or `--watch`.

### Preflight checks

Every `promptise run` checks the project before it starts the program, and lists *every* problem it found instead of failing on the first one at runtime:

- the manifest is valid;
- every `-e K=V` is well formed, every `--env-file` exists, and every env file can be read and is safe to load;
- every variable in `[env] required` is set;
- the entry exists: the `main` file, or the agent factory for the agent modes.

If anything is wrong, it exits with code 2 and starts nothing.

`--check` runs the same checks and also checks the entry itself: a script must compile, and a factory's module must import and define the factory. Then it exits: 0 when the project is ready, 2 when it is not. Importing a factory module runs its module-level code; a script is only compiled, never run.

The factory is imported the way the real run imports it: the project root and the `python_path` entries come first on `sys.path`. A factory in a package (`agent = "customer_agent.agent:create_agent"`) passes `--check` from any directory of the project.

```bash
promptise run --check                    # main
promptise run --mode chat --check        # the agent factory
promptise run --prod --serve --check     # what the container will run
```

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | The program finished, or the server shut down cleanly |
| `1` | A runtime error: an uncaught exception, a factory that failed to build the agent, a port that is in use |
| `2` | A configuration or usage error: an invalid manifest, a missing variable, an unknown target, a failed check, a public host without a token |
| `130` | Interrupted with Ctrl+C |
| `143` | Stopped by SIGTERM (script mode, with `--prod`) |

In script mode, `sys.exit(code)` in your program sets the code.

---

## Serve mode

```bash
promptise run --serve                       # 127.0.0.1:8080, from [serve]
promptise run --serve --port 9000
promptise run --prod --serve --host 0.0.0.0 # in a container (needs a token)
```

`--serve` builds the agent from the factory and answers HTTP requests. One agent serves every request.

| Method and path | Auth | Response |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /healthz` | none | `200 {"status": "ok"}` while the process runs (liveness) |
| `GET /readyz` | none | `200 {"status": "ready"}` once the agent is built; `503` before that (`not_ready`) and while shutting down (`draining`) (readiness) |
| `GET /v1/info` | bearer | The project (name, version, model, ...) and the agent's tool names |
| `POST /v1/invoke` | bearer | Runs the agent: `{"output", "duration_ms", "usage", "request_id"}` |
| `POST /v1/stream` | bearer | Runs the agent and streams Server-Sent Events, one `data: <JSON>` line per event |

The request body of `/v1/invoke` and `/v1/stream` is a JSON object:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `input` | string, or a list of messages | The question, or the conversation as `[{"role": "user", "content": "..."}]` |
| `session_id` | string, optional | 1 to 256 letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `:` or `-` |

With a string `input` and a `session_id`, an agent built with a `conversation_store` loads and saves the conversation of that session, so the client sends only the new message. Otherwise nothing is stored: with a list of messages, the client owns the history. See [Conversations](conversations.md).

```bash
curl -s localhost:8080/healthz
curl -s localhost:8080/v1/info

curl -s localhost:8080/v1/invoke \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input": "Where is my order A1002?"}'
```

```json
{
  "output": "Your order A1002 is in transit with DHL and should arrive on 2026-10-19.",
  "duration_ms": 2140.5,
  "usage": {"llm_calls": 2, "prompt_tokens": 1630, "completion_tokens": 58, "total_tokens": 1688},
  "request_id": "6f1d0c9e2a7b4c1e"
}
```

`usage` counts the tokens of every model call the request made, as the model reported them (zeros when it reports none).

```bash
curl -N localhost:8080/v1/stream \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input": "Where is my order A1002?"}'
```

Each streamed event is a [streaming event](streaming.md) as JSON. Its `type` is `token`, `tool_start` or `tool_end`, and the stream ends with `done` (which also carries `usage`) or `error`:

```text
data: {"type": "tool_start", "tool_name": "lookup_order", "arguments": {"order_id": "A1002"}, ...}
data: {"type": "tool_end", "tool_name": "lookup_order", "success": true, "duration_ms": 3.1, ...}
data: {"type": "token", "text": "Your order", ...}
data: {"type": "done", "full_response": "Your order A1002 is in transit ...", "usage": {...}, ...}
```

A streamed request with a stored session (`session_id` on an agent with a `conversation_store`) sends the whole answer as one `token` event, then `done`.

Every response has an `X-Request-ID` header: the one the client sent, when it is well formed, or a new one.

### Authentication

When the variable named by `[serve] auth_token_env` (default `PROMPTISE_SERVE_TOKEN`) is set, every `/v1/*` request must send it as a bearer token, or it gets `401`. `/healthz` and `/readyz` never need one, so probes work without it. Use a long random token: a token shorter than 16 characters logs a warning.

```bash
export PROMPTISE_SERVE_TOKEN="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
promptise run --serve

curl -s localhost:8080/v1/invoke \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PROMPTISE_SERVE_TOKEN" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input": "Where is my order A1002?"}'
```

On a host that is not a loopback address (`--host 0.0.0.0`, say), `promptise run` refuses to start without a token (exit code 2).

Without a token, on a loopback address, `/v1/*` refuses a request whose `Host` header is not a loopback name (`421`) or that carries a cross-site `Origin` (`403`). A web page open in your browser cannot drive the agent.

### Errors

Errors are JSON: `{"error": "<message>"}`.

| Status | When |
|---|---|
| `400` | The body is not a JSON object, has unknown fields, or has an invalid `input` or `session_id` |
| `401` | A token is set and the request has no valid bearer token |
| `403`, `421` | No token is set and the request comes from a browser page or a non-loopback `Host` |
| `429` | `{"error": "busy"}`: `max_concurrency` requests are already running (with `Retry-After`) |
| `500` | `{"error": "internal error", "error_id": "..."}`: the agent failed. The exception is logged with the same `error_id`, never sent to the client |
| `503` | `{"error": "draining"}`: the server is shutting down |

### Limits and shutdown

- At most `[serve] max_concurrency` requests (default 8) run at the same time. A request beyond that gets `429` at once.
- On SIGTERM (or Ctrl+C) the server drains: `/readyz` and new `/v1/*` requests answer `503`, and requests already running get up to `[prod] shutdown_timeout` seconds to finish. Then the process exits with 0.

The API serves one agent for one application. To give each of your users their own identity, conversations and permissions, embed the agent in your own web server instead.

---

## Deploy with Docker

```dockerfile
FROM python:3.12-slim

WORKDIR /app
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir promptise
COPY . .

# The environment comes from the container, not from a .env file.
ENV PROMPTISE_NO_DOTENV=1

EXPOSE 8080
CMD ["promptise", "run", "--prod", "--serve", "--host", "0.0.0.0"]
```

Pass the API key and the serve token as environment variables, not in the image:

```bash
docker build -t support-bot .
docker run -p 8080:8080 \
  -e OPENAI_API_KEY \
  -e PROMPTISE_SERVE_TOKEN \
  support-bot
```

Because the host is `0.0.0.0`, the container refuses to start without `PROMPTISE_SERVE_TOKEN`. Point the liveness probe at `/healthz` and the readiness probe at `/readyz`. The container stops gracefully on SIGTERM, which is what `docker stop` and Kubernetes send.

Add a `.dockerignore` with `.env` so your local secrets never end up in the image. To check a project before you deploy it, run `promptise run --prod --check` in CI with the same environment variables.

---

## Migrating from `promptise run --model-id`

The inline REPL still works unchanged:

```bash
promptise run --model-id openai:gpt-5-mini \
    --http "name=tools url=http://localhost:8000/mcp"
```

`--model-id`, `--stdio`, `--http`, `--instructions`, `--trace/--no-trace` and `--raw/--no-raw` select it, exactly as in 1.3. You do not need to change anything.

To move the same setup into a project, put the servers in a factory:

```python
from promptise import PromptiseAgent, build_agent
from promptise.config import HTTPServerSpec
from promptise.run import RunContext


async def create_agent(ctx: RunContext) -> PromptiseAgent:
    return await build_agent(
        model=ctx.model or "openai:gpt-5-mini",
        servers={"tools": HTTPServerSpec(url="http://localhost:8000/mcp")},
    )
```

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `promptise run --model-id M --http "..."` | `promptise run agent.py:create_agent` (chat mode), or `promptise run --mode chat` with `agent = "agent.py:create_agent"` in the manifest |
| `--model-id M` | `--model M` (overrides the model of every agent) |
| `--instructions "..."` | `instructions=` in `build_agent()` |
| `--trace` | `--devtools` |

---

## Flag reference

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `TARGET` | A script name, a `.py` file, `file.py:factory` or `package.module:factory` (default: `main`) |
| `ARGS` | Arguments for the program (`sys.argv[1:]`) or appended to a script; `--` ends the options |
| `-d`, `--devtools` | [Dev tools](#dev-tools): live trace on stderr and a summary at the end |
| `-t`, `-tui`, `--tui` | [The terminal UI](#the-terminal-ui) |
| `-w`, `--watch` | [Restart on file changes](#watch-mode) |
| `--prod` | [Production behavior](#production); not with `--tui` or `--watch` |
| `--check` | Check the project and the entry, then exit 0 (ready) or 2 |
| `--mode MODE` | `auto` (default), `script`, `chat`, `once` or `serve` |
| `--serve` | Short for `--mode serve` |
| `-i TEXT`, `--input TEXT` | Ask one question (once mode); `-` reads it from stdin |
| `--json` | Once mode: print the answer and stats as JSON |
| `--host HOST` | Serve mode: the address (overrides `[serve] host`) |
| `-p PORT`, `--port PORT` | Serve mode: the port (overrides `[serve] port`) |
| `--env-file PATH` | Load this `.env`-style file before the `[env] files` (repeatable) |
| `-e K=V`, `--env K=V` | Set a variable for this run, overriding the environment (repeatable) |
| `--model MODEL` | Use this model for every agent |
| `--observe LEVEL` | Override `[dev] observe` or `[prod] observe` |
| `--report PATH` | Write a JSON run report on exit |
| `--list` | List the scripts |
| `-f PATH`, `--manifest PATH` | Use this manifest |

# Promptise CLI Reference

The `promptise` CLI provides commands for running your project (`run`), creating one (`init --project`), listing tools, running interactive agent sessions, serving an MCP server from a module (`serve`), turning an existing API into an MCP server (`mcpcast`), checking model providers (`models`), verifying audit logs (`audit verify`), and managing runtime processes.

```bash
promptise --version
```

---

## Global Options

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--version` | Print version and exit |
| `--help` | Show help for any command |

---

## `promptise list-tools` -- List Available Tools

Discover tools exposed by MCP servers without writing code.

```bash
# List tools from an HTTP MCP server
promptise list-tools --model-id openai:gpt-5-mini --http "name=my_tools url=http://localhost:8000/mcp"

# List tools from a stdio MCP server
promptise list-tools --model-id openai:gpt-5-mini --stdio "name=echo command=python args='-m mytools.server'"
```

### Options

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--model-id` | LLM model identifier (required, e.g. `openai:gpt-5-mini`) |
| `--stdio` | Add a stdio MCP server (repeatable) |
| `--http` | Add an HTTP MCP server (repeatable) |
| `--instructions` | Optional system prompt override |

### Server Spec Syntax

Both `--stdio` and `--http` accept a quoted string of `key=value` pairs:

**HTTP servers:**

```bash
--http "name=my_tools url=http://localhost:8000/mcp"
```

| Key | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | yes | Server name (used as identifier) |
| `url` | yes | HTTP endpoint URL |

**Stdio servers:**

```bash
--stdio "name=echo command=python args='-m mytools.server --port 3333' env.API_KEY=xyz"
```

| Key | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | yes | Server name |
| `command` | yes | Executable to run |
| `args` | no | Command arguments (quote for spaces) |
| `env.*` | no | Environment variables (e.g. `env.API_KEY=xyz`) |
| `cwd` | no | Working directory |

Repeat `--stdio` or `--http` for multiple servers.

---

## `promptise run` -- Run Your Project

Run your project's program, like `npm start`. The project is described by `promptise.toml` (or `[tool.promptise]` in `pyproject.toml`), found from the current directory upwards. `promptise run` runs the manifest's `main` file as a normal Python program and instruments every agent it builds, with no changes to your code. See [Projects & promptise run](projects.md) for the manifest and every mode.

```bash
promptise run [TARGET] [ARGS]... [OPTIONS]
```

```bash
promptise run                          # run `main`, like `python main.py`
promptise run main.py "a question"     # pass arguments to the program
promptise run dev                      # a script from [scripts], like `npm run dev`
promptise run --devtools               # live traces, tool calls, tokens and cost
promptise run --tui                    # the full terminal UI
promptise run --watch                  # restart on file changes
promptise run --prod                   # JSON logs, preflight checks, graceful SIGTERM
promptise run --serve                  # an HTTP API for the agent factory
promptise run -i "a question"          # ask the agent factory one question
promptise run agent.py:create_agent    # chat with the agent a factory builds
promptise run --list                   # list the scripts
```

`TARGET` is a script name from `[scripts]`, a `.py` file, `file.py:factory` or `package.module:factory`. Without one, `promptise run` runs the manifest's `main`. `ARGS` become the program's `sys.argv[1:]`, or are appended to a script's command; put `--` before arguments that look like options.

### Options

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `-d`, `--devtools` | Live trace of every agent on stderr, and a summary at the end. Tool calls refused before they ran (autonomy budget, approval denial) are printed as `⊘ <tool> refused` with the reason, and counted as `refused` in the summary |
| `-t`, `-tui`, `--tui` | Open the terminal UI |
| `-w`, `--watch` | Restart the program when a project file changes |
| `--prod` | Production behavior: JSON logs on stderr, preflight checks, graceful SIGTERM |
| `--check` | Check the project and the entry, then exit (0 ready, 2 not ready). A factory is imported with the project root and `python_path` on `sys.path`, as in a real run |
| `--mode` | `auto` (default), `script`, `chat`, `once` or `serve` |
| `--serve` | Serve the agent factory over HTTP (`--mode serve`) |
| `-i`, `--input` | Ask the agent factory one question and print the answer (`-` reads stdin) |
| `--json` | With `-i`: print the answer and stats as JSON |
| `--host` | Serve mode: the address (default from `[serve] host`, `127.0.0.1`) |
| `-p`, `--port` | Serve mode: the port (default from `[serve] port`, `8080`) |
| `--env-file` | Load this `.env`-style file before the manifest's `[env] files` (repeatable) |
| `-e`, `--env` | Set a variable for this run, `K=V`, overriding the environment (repeatable) |
| `--model` | Use this model for every agent the program builds |
| `--observe` | Recording level: `off`, `basic`, `standard` or `full` |
| `--report` | Write a JSON run report to this path on exit |
| `--list` | List the scripts in the manifest |
| `-f`, `--manifest` | Use this manifest instead of searching for one |

Exit codes: `0` success, `1` runtime error, `2` configuration or usage error (also a failed `--check`), `130` interrupted with Ctrl+C, `143` stopped by SIGTERM (a script under `--prod`). `--prod` cannot be combined with `--tui` or `--watch`.

### Inline REPL (`--model-id`)

The inline REPL from earlier versions works unchanged. Any of its flags selects it: start an interactive session with inline MCP server specs, with no project and no `.superagent` file.

```bash
promptise run --model-id openai:gpt-5-mini \
    --http "name=tools url=http://localhost:8000/mcp"
```

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--model-id` | LLM model identifier (required, e.g. `openai:gpt-5-mini`) |
| `--stdio` | Add a stdio MCP server (repeatable) |
| `--http` | Add an HTTP MCP server (repeatable) |
| `--instructions` | Optional system prompt override |
| `--trace/--no-trace` | Print tool invocations and results (default: `--trace`) |
| `--raw/--no-raw` | Also print raw result object (default: `--no-raw`) |

To move an inline session into a project, see [Migrating from `promptise run --model-id`](projects.md#migrating-from-promptise-run-model-id).

---

## `promptise agent` -- Agent from .superagent File

Run an interactive agent session from a `.superagent` configuration file. CLI flags override file settings.

```bash
# From a .superagent file
promptise agent config.superagent

# Override model
promptise agent config.superagent --model-id openai:gpt-5-mini

# With additional servers from CLI
promptise agent config.superagent --http "name=extra url=http://localhost:9000/mcp"
```

### Options

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--model-id` | Override model from config file |
| `--instructions` | Override instructions from config file |
| `--trace/--no-trace` | Override trace setting from config file |
| `--stdio` | Additional stdio server (merged with config file servers) |
| `--http` | Additional HTTP server (merged with config file servers) |
| `--raw/--no-raw` | Also print raw result object |

---

## `promptise validate` -- Validate .superagent File

Validate a `.superagent` configuration file without building the agent.

```bash
# Full validation
promptise validate my_agent.superagent

# Skip environment variable checks
promptise validate my_agent.superagent --no-check-env

# Skip cross-agent reference checks
promptise validate my_agent.superagent --no-check-refs
```

### Options

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--check-env/--no-check-env` | Check environment variable availability, for the file and every cross-agent file (default: `--check-env`) |
| `--allow-missing-env` | Report a missing environment variable as a warning instead of failing |
| `--check-refs/--no-check-refs` | Validate cross-agent references at every depth (default: `--check-refs`) |

Performs YAML syntax checks, schema validation, environment variable availability checks, and cross-agent reference validation. Exits with code 1 when anything fails, including a missing environment variable; in CI where the secrets are not set, pass `--allow-missing-env` (warn) or `--no-check-env` (skip).

---

## `promptise init` -- Generate a Template or a Project

### `promptise init --project` -- Create a Project

Create a new project for [`promptise run`](projects.md): a manifest, an agent factory and a program that uses it.

```bash
promptise init --project [DIR] [--name NAME] [--model MODEL] [--force]
```

```bash
# A project in a new directory
promptise init --project my-bot

# The current directory, with an Anthropic model
promptise init --project --model anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-5

# Then
cd my-bot
cp .env.example .env    # set the API key
promptise run
```

It writes `promptise.toml`, `agent.py` (the `create_agent` factory, with one local tool), `main.py` (a normal script that asks the agent one question), `.env.example` and `README.md`, and adds `.env`, `.promptise/` and `__pycache__/` to `.gitignore` without duplicating lines. Existing files are never overwritten without `--force`: every conflict is listed and nothing is written. Nothing is fetched from the network.

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `DIR` | Where to create the project (default: the current directory; created if missing) |
| `--project` | Create a project instead of a `.superagent` file |
| `--name` | The project name (default: the directory's name) |
| `--model` | The model string (default: `openai:gpt-5-mini`). Also sets `[env] required` to that provider's API key |
| `--force` | Overwrite existing files |

### `promptise init` -- Generate a .superagent File

Without `--project`, create a starter `.superagent` configuration file with common patterns.

```bash
# Basic template
promptise init

# HTTP server template with auth headers
promptise init --output api_agent.superagent --template http

# Full-featured template
promptise init -o advanced.superagent -t advanced --force
```

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--output`, `-o` | Output file path (default: `agent.superagent`) |
| `--template`, `-t` | Template type: `basic`, `http`, `stdio`, `cross-agent`, `advanced` |
| `--force/--no-force` | Overwrite existing files |

Every template uses `openai:gpt-5-mini` and passes `promptise validate <file> --allow-missing-env`
as generated (without the flag, `validate` lists the `${VAR}`s you still have to set).
`cross-agent` and `advanced` also write the specialist files their `cross_agents` section names,
in `agents/` next to the output file: `math_agent.superagent` and `research_agent.superagent`,
or `specialist_a.superagent` and `specialist_b.superagent`. An existing file is never
overwritten without `--force`.

---

## `promptise serve` -- Run an MCP Server

Run an `MCPServer` from a Python module over stdio, HTTP or SSE -- the MCP equivalent of `uvicorn myapp:app`. The target is `module.path:attribute`; the CLI imports it, checks that it is an `MCPServer` instance (exit code 1 otherwise) and serves it.

```bash
# stdio, for Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Cursor
promptise serve myapp.server:server

# HTTP on the loopback address, with the live dashboard
promptise serve myapp.server:server -t http --port 8080 --dashboard

# A public bind behind a gateway: name the hosts (and browser origins) you serve
promptise serve myapp.server:server -t http --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --allowed-host api.example.com --allowed-origin https://app.example.com

# Development: restart on source changes
promptise serve myapp.server:server -t http --reload
```

### Options

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `TARGET` (argument) | `module.path:attribute` naming the `MCPServer` instance (e.g. `myapp.server:server`) |
| `--transport`, `-t` | `stdio` (default), `http`, or `sse` |
| `--host` | Bind host for HTTP/SSE (default: `127.0.0.1`) |
| `--port`, `-p` | Bind port for HTTP/SSE (default: `8080`) |
| `--dashboard` | Live terminal dashboard (HTTP/SSE only; a warning is printed with `stdio`, whose terminal is the protocol stream) |
| `--reload` | Hot-reload on source changes (development only) |
| `--allowed-host HOST` | `Host` header value to accept on HTTP/SSE, e.g. `api.example.com` or `api.example.com:*` (repeatable). A loopback bind validates `Host` and `Origin` against the loopback names by default and the list **adds** to them (a reverse proxy forwarding the public `Host` to `127.0.0.1`); a non-loopback bind has no restriction until this names the hosts it serves |
| `--allowed-origin ORIGIN` | `Origin` header value to accept for browser clients, e.g. `https://app.example.com` (repeatable). Requests without an `Origin` header (every non-browser MCP client) always pass. Requires `--allowed-host` on a non-loopback bind |

See [Deployment](../mcp/server/deployment.md#host-and-origin-validation) for what the validation protects against (DNS rebinding), the reverse-proxy setup and the CORS configuration that complements it.

---

## `promptise mcpcast` -- Generate an MCP Server from an API

Turn an existing API (OpenAPI 3.x or Swagger 2) into a curated, safe, agent-ready MCP server, emitted as editable code. The command parses the spec, classifies every operation's risk (`read`, `write`, `destructive`, `financial`), designs the tool surface (with a model, or deterministically with `--no-curate`), and writes `<name>-mcp/`: `mcpcast.plan.yaml` (the editable source of truth), the server as an installable `<name>_mcp/` package (config, HTTP client, approval gate, one tools module per resource — regenerated from the plan), a `server.py` launcher, a `tests/` suite, `README.md` (Claude Desktop / Claude Code / Cursor install snippets), and — written once — `pyproject.toml`, `Dockerfile`, `.env.example` and `.gitignore`. Read-only by default: write, destructive and financial tools are only generated under `--profile standard` / `full`, and every non-read tool is approval-gated server-side by `ApprovalGateMiddleware`.

```bash
# No arguments: the guided setup — a full-screen terminal wizard
promptise mcpcast

# Deterministic, fully offline: one read tool per GET operation
promptise mcpcast openapi.yaml --no-curate

# LLM-curated surface, reads + approval-gated writes, review the plan before writing
promptise mcpcast https://api.example.com/openapi.json --profile standard --review

# Everything exposed, API-key auth for MCP clients, then score it with a real agent
promptise mcpcast openapi.yaml --profile full --auth api-key --eval

# Regenerate server.py next to an edited plan, then serve a fresh one over HTTP
promptise mcpcast mcpcast.plan.yaml
promptise mcpcast openapi.yaml --no-curate --serve -t http
```

### Options

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `SPEC` (argument) | OpenAPI spec as a file path, URL, or inline JSON -- or an existing `mcpcast.plan.yaml` to regenerate the server from an edited plan. **Omit it to open the [guided setup](../mcpcast/guided-setup.md)**, a full-screen terminal wizard that collects every option below |
| `--interactive`, `-i` | Open the guided setup pre-filled with `SPEC`, `--base-url`, `--out`, `--model`, `--eval-tasks` and `--force`. Every other flag is refused together with it -- choose it in the wizard. Without a terminal (CI, a pipe) the wizard exits with code 1 and prints the non-interactive form to run |
| `--output`, `--out`, `-o` | Output directory (default: `./<name>-mcp`, or the plan's own directory when `SPEC` is a `mcpcast.plan.yaml`). A directory that already has files in it -- an mcpcast project or anything else -- is refused without `--force` |
| `--force` | Write into an output directory that already has files in it: an existing mcpcast project (so an edited plan is never replaced by a re-derived one without saying so) or any other non-empty directory, whose `README.md`, `server.py`, `tests/` and package would be replaced |
| `--base-url` | API base URL; required when the spec declares no absolute server URL and was not fetched from a URL it can be resolved against |
| `--profile` | Safety profile: `read-only` (default), `standard`, `full` |
| `--auth` | Upstream auth: `passthrough` (default; each caller forwards its own `Authorization` header over HTTP/SSE), `env-token` (one credential from `MCPCAST_UPSTREAM_TOKEN` — for stdio/desktop clients; binds loopback only unless `--public`), `api-key` (per-tenant upstream tokens), `none` (no credentials, loopback only unless `--public`) |
| `--approval` | Who approves gated calls: `elicitation`, `pending` (default: `pending` with `--auth api-key`, `elicitation` otherwise) |
| `--name` | Server name (default: derived from the spec title) |
| `--curate/--no-curate` | LLM-assisted tool design (default: `--curate`); `--no-curate` is fully offline and maps one tool per operation |
| `--model` | Model for curation and `--eval` (default: `openai:gpt-5-mini`). Any provider string works -- `azure:chat-prod`, `foundry:Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct`, `bedrock:...` -- see [`promptise models`](#promptise-models-model-providers) |
| `--max-tools` | Tool budget (default: 25 with curation; unlimited with `--no-curate`) |
| `--review` | Print the kept / not-exposed tables and confirm before writing. Every cell that comes from the spec, the plan or the model (tool names, descriptions, paths, parameter names, operation ids, drop reasons) is rendered inert: Rich markup is escaped and terminal control characters (ESC, the C1 range, DEL) become spaces, so a hostile spec cannot blank or rewrite the row of a destructive tool before you confirm |
| `--yes`, `-y` | With `--review`: write without asking |
| `--eval` | Score the generated server with a real agent (Agent Readiness Score); writes `eval/tasks.yaml` and `eval/report.md`. When live reads would go out with the placeholder credential a hint asks for `MCPCAST_EVAL_AUTHORIZATION`; an existing `MCPCAST_UPSTREAM_TOKEN` (env-token) or an `MCPCAST_UPSTREAM_TOKENS` entry for the evaluation tenant `mcpcast-eval` (api-key) counts as configured, as does `MCPCAST_EVAL_HEADERS` |
| `--eval-tasks` | Number of tasks to generate for `--eval` (default: `20`) |
| `--serve` | Run the generated server immediately after writing it |
| `--transport`, `-t` | With `--serve`: `stdio` (default), `http`, or `sse` |
| `--host` | With `--serve`: bind host for HTTP/SSE (default: `127.0.0.1`) |
| `--port`, `-p` | With `--serve`: bind port for HTTP/SSE (default: `8080`) |
| `--public` | With `--serve`: let an `env-token` or `none` server bind a non-loopback address. Such a server has no MCP-level authentication and acts with the operator's credential -- only behind an authenticating gateway. Refused with exit code 2 without `--serve`, and -- once the plan is known, before anything is written -- for an `api-key` or `passthrough` project (`--public only applies to --auth env-token / none; this project uses api-key, which already binds any host`): those modes authenticate every caller and have no such switch |

**Plain-http upstreams.** When the plan's `base_url` (or an operation-level server) is a non-loopback `http://` host and the auth mode carries a credential (`env-token`, `api-key`, `passthrough`), the summary is followed by a yellow warning naming the hosts: the generated server refuses every call to them with `UPSTREAM_INSECURE` until `MCPCAST_ALLOW_INSECURE_HTTP=1` is set where it runs (an intranet or staging API), or the plan points at an `https://` base URL. With `--auth none` no credential travels and nothing is said.

**Fetching the spec from a URL.** A URL `SPEC` may carry a credential for the download only -- `https://user:token@host/openapi.json` is sent as HTTP Basic auth, and `?api_key=...` reaches the server as typed. Nothing derived from that URL keeps it: the plan's `base_url` (when the spec declares no `servers`, the API is taken to live at the URL's origin), `spec_source`, the server name and the `Parsed ... from` line all use the URL without its userinfo, query string and fragment. A `base_url` that carries `user:password@` -- on `--base-url` or in a hand-edited plan -- is refused with a pointer at `--auth env-token` and `MCPCAST_UPSTREAM_TOKEN`, the supported way to give the generated server an upstream credential. The download is bounded three ways: `MCPCAST_MAX_SPEC_BYTES` (default 20 MiB, checked before the body is buffered), `MCPCAST_FETCH_SECONDS` (default 60; a wall-clock deadline for the whole download, since a server that trickles bytes would otherwise never trip httpx's per-read timeout) and `MCPCAST_MAX_SPEC_NODES` (default 2,000,000 nodes after YAML aliases are expanded, which is what turns a 1 KB alias bomb into gigabytes). Exceeding any of them prints `Error:` naming the variable to raise.

**Regenerating from a plan.** Pass `mcpcast.plan.yaml` as `SPEC` (a path, a URL or inline text — recognised by shape; an inline plan of any length is written into `./<name>-mcp` and shown as `Regenerating from plan <inline>`, never echoed) to rebuild the package, `server.py`, `tests/` and `README.md` next to it from the edited plan without re-curating (a plan fetched from a URL is written into `./<name>-mcp`); the plan file itself is not rewritten (comments survive), and neither are the scaffold files (`pyproject.toml`, `Dockerfile`, `.env.example`, `.gitignore`) once they exist. Tools modules the plan no longer produces are removed. Spec-only flags (`--profile`, `--auth`, `--approval`, `--base-url`, `--name`, `--max-tools`) are rejected with exit code 2 in this mode -- change those values in the plan file instead. With `--eval` the spec recorded in the plan is re-read for realistic mocks.

**Exit codes and output.** An invalid option exits with code 2; a spec, plan, curation or model failure (a missing provider key, an unimportable generated server) prints `Error: ...` and exits with code 1 (if curation fails after its retries, re-run with `--no-curate`); aborting at the `--review` prompt exits with code 1 without writing. A document that is OpenAPI-shaped but broken never produces a traceback: a defect of the whole document (`info` or `paths` that is not a mapping, nesting deeper than 256 levels, more than 2,000,000 nodes once YAML aliases are expanded) is an `Error:`, while a defect inside one operation (`parameters` that is not a list of mappings, a `requestBody.content` or schema that is a string) drops only that operation, with the reason recorded under `dropped:` in the plan; `operationId: 5` is read as `"5"` and `tags` that are not a list are ignored. All progress -- including the model calls of curation and `--eval` -- is printed to stderr, so with `--serve` over `stdio` stdout stays clean as the MCP protocol stream. `--serve` goes through the generated entry point, so an `--auth none` server still refuses a non-loopback `--host`.

See the [MCPcast guide](../mcp/server/mcpcast.md) for safety profiles, auth modes and the generated server's runtime contract, and the [MCPcast API reference](../api/mcpcast.md) for the Python API.

---

## `promptise models` -- Model Providers

Every place Promptise takes a model -- `build_agent(model=...)`, `.superagent` and `.agent` files, `promptise mcpcast --model`, `--model-id` on `run` / `agent` / `list-tools` -- accepts one `provider:model` string, and every string goes through the same registry (`promptise.models`). The `models` subcommand group shows that registry, diagnoses one string before you put it in a config file, and prints the environment variables a provider needs. Friendly aliases are accepted everywhere: `azure:` for Azure OpenAI, `foundry:` for the Azure AI Foundry model catalog, `gemini:`, `vertex:`, `bedrock:`, `mistral:`, `grok:`, `hf:`.

```bash
# Every provider: prefixes and aliases, install status, which env vars are set
promptise models list

# What one string resolves to and what is missing to use it (exit 1 if not usable).
# Configuration only -- except that a local or keyless server (Ollama, a vLLM on
# localhost) is checked for a listener, since it has no credential to check
promptise models check azure:chat-prod

# The same, plus a real one-token call to the model
promptise models check openai:gpt-5-mini --ping

# Export lines for a provider, with placeholders and where to find each value
promptise models env azure
```

### Subcommands

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `models list` | Table of every provider: the `provider=` name with its aliases, its route (`native` — the core integration — or `OpenAI-compatible`), whether its required env vars are `set` / `missing` / `none required`, and an example model string. Nothing needs installing for any row. |
| `models check <provider:model> [--ping]` | Explains what the string resolves to (alias → canonical name), what the model part means for that provider (a deployment name on Azure, a model id elsewhere), the route it will use (the exact OpenAI-compatible URL with the endpoint, region and project filled in from the environment -- `http://localhost:11434/v1` for a default Ollama -- or the native integration), each env var with its state -- `set`, `set (from /path/.env)` when the `.env` file supplied it, `MISSING`, `MISSING (VAR is exported but empty — unset it or give it a value)`, `unset (optional)` -- and where to find its value, and the provider's notes. When the string is not usable, every problem is listed with its fix (`  - ...` lines, the same text `build_agent()` puts in its `ModelSetupError`). Otherwise it prints `Configuration OK` -- the settings are in place, which is not the same as a working model: nothing is called. For a keyless provider (Ollama) or an endpoint on this machine (`OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8000/v1`) it also tries a TCP connection (1 s timeout, nothing is sent) and reports `Not reachable.` with what to try (`nothing is listening at http://localhost:11434 — is Ollama running? (ollama serve) ...`) when nothing answers. `--ping` additionally makes a real one-token call; when it fails, the provider's error is followed by a `→` line saying what it most likely means: nothing listening, a timeout, a rejected key (naming the variable), a model or deployment that does not exist (`ollama pull <model>` for Ollama), missing model access, an account out of credits, a rate limit or a provider outage. |
| `models env <provider>` | Prints `export` lines for the provider's env vars with example values and a hint per line — paste them into `.env`. Any name or alias works (`azure`, `aoai`, `bedrock`). |

**Exit codes.** `models check` exits with `1` when the string is not usable yet (a required env var unset, or `native=True` without its package), when a local or keyless server is not listening, or when the `--ping` call fails -- so it works as a preflight step in CI and container entrypoints; `0` when the configuration is complete (and, for a local server, something is listening). `models env` exits with `2` for an unknown provider. `models list` always exits `0`.

With nothing configured, `promptise models check azure:chat-prod` prints:

```text
$ promptise models check azure:chat-prod
azure:chat-prod → azure_openai:chat-prod  (Azure OpenAI (OpenAI models deployed in Azure AI Foundry))
  model part: chat-prod — in the string form, your DEPLOYMENT name (Foundry → Deployments → Name); with Model(...), the model name (gpt-4o); the deployment goes in deployment=
  route: native integration (core)
  AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT: MISSING — Azure AI Foundry portal → your resource → Overview → Endpoint (https://<resource>.openai.azure.com/, no path)
  AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY: MISSING — Azure AI Foundry portal → your resource → Keys and Endpoint → KEY 1 (or Entra ID: pass extra={'azure_ad_token_provider': ...})
  OPENAI_API_VERSION: MISSING — the REST API version your deployment supports, e.g. 2024-10-21 (Azure docs → 'API version lifecycle')
  Azure routes requests by deployment name, not model name: Model('gpt-4o', provider='azure', deployment='chat-prod', ...).
Not usable yet.
  - AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT is not set: Azure AI Foundry portal → your resource → Overview → Endpoint (https://<resource>.openai.azure.com/, no path) (e.g. https://my-resource.openai.azure.com/)
  - AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY is not set: Azure AI Foundry portal → your resource → Keys and Endpoint → KEY 1 (or Entra ID: pass extra={'azure_ad_token_provider': ...})
  - OPENAI_API_VERSION is not set: the REST API version your deployment supports, e.g. 2024-10-21 (Azure docs → 'API version lifecycle') (e.g. 2024-10-21)
  - put AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT, AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_VERSION in a .env file next to your script (loaded automatically; a variable already exported with a non-empty value wins, an empty one is filled from the file), export it, or pass it in code: Model(..., endpoint=, api_key=, api_version=). See promptise models env azure
$ echo $?
1
```

On a machine where Ollama is not running, `promptise models check ollama:llama3.1` says so instead of passing:

```text
$ promptise models check ollama:llama3.1
ollama:llama3.1 → ollama:llama3.1  (Ollama (local models))
  model part: llama3.1 — a model you have pulled (`ollama pull llama3.1`)
  route: OpenAI-compatible endpoint http://localhost:11434/v1 (core, nothing to install)
  OLLAMA_HOST: unset (optional) — only if Ollama is not on the default http://localhost:11434
  No API key. The model must support tool calling to drive MCP tools.
Not reachable. The configuration is complete, but nothing is listening at http://localhost:11434 — is Ollama running? (ollama serve) If it runs on another host or port, set OLLAMA_HOST.
$ echo $?
1
```

and `--ping` against a server that is down names the cause after the error:

```text
Pinging… failed
OpenAIConnectionError: Connection error.
  → nothing is listening at http://localhost:11434 — is Ollama running? (ollama serve) If it runs on another host or port, set OLLAMA_HOST.
```

A variable that is exported but empty (`export OPENAI_API_KEY=` left in a shell profile) is reported as such -- `OPENAI_API_KEY: MISSING (OPENAI_API_KEY is exported but empty — unset it or give it a value)` -- and one the `.env` file filled names the file: `OPENAI_API_KEY: set (from /home/me/project/.env)`.

`promptise models env azure` then gives you the three lines to fill in:

```text
$ promptise models env azure
# Azure OpenAI (OpenAI models deployed in Azure AI Foundry) — model string example: azure:chat-prod
export AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT=https://my-resource.openai.azure.com/
#   ↳ Azure AI Foundry portal → your resource → Overview → Endpoint (https://<resource>.openai.azure.com/, no path)
export AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY=...
#   ↳ Azure AI Foundry portal → your resource → Keys and Endpoint → KEY 1 (or Entra ID: pass extra={'azure_ad_token_provider': ...})
export OPENAI_API_VERSION=2024-10-21
#   ↳ the REST API version your deployment supports, e.g. 2024-10-21 (Azure docs → 'API version lifecycle')
```

The same checks run inside `build_agent()`: a string that `models check` reports as not usable raises a `ModelSetupError` with the same text instead of a provider stack trace. See [Model Setup](../getting-started/model-setup.md) for every provider and the [Models API reference](../api/models.md) for `resolve_model()` / `check_model()`.
